title: Ivo and the Drop
premise: Silas Voss, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call he failed to save, is summoned when Flight 447 disappears from every radar, database, and memory of official record while still airborne. The plane is carrying a defector with proof that a joint intelligence program called DROP has been selling assassination targets to the highest bidder. Silas must broker the truth past three governments and an assassin codenamed Lark, aided by Ada Reyes, the flight's air marshal and his former lover, whose duty demands she silence the very witness Silas has sworn to protect. In the end, Silas trades his own freedom for the broadcast of the evidence, exposing DROP but surrendering himself to the consequences he once escaped.
about_author: Mirabel Zhou is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent six years reconstructing accident timelines for claims no one wanted paid. She writes thrillers about paper trails and the people who burn them.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Silas Voss negotiates a bank hostage crisis with flawless calm, then goes home to a packed bag and a framed photo of the negotiation that killed a girl named Tessa. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: competence as armor over guilt.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Air marshal Ada Reyes boards a red-eye carrying Marcus Hale, a nervous defector clutching an encrypted drive. She notices two passengers who board without tickets appearing in the manifest. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: professional suspicion sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Mid-flight, every record of Flight 447 evaporates: radar logs, booking data, crew rosters. The plane lands at Dulles to a closed gate and men waiting. POV: alternating Silas (summoned) and Ada (detained). Emotional beat: reality itself feels edited.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Silas is briefed by handler Odile Ferrant: officially, Flight 447 never existed. He recognizes the erasure signature — the same one from his buried failure years ago. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the past reaching up through the floor.

chapters.title: Hale in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ada escapes custody during transfer, dragging a sedated Hale through airport service tunnels. She calls the only number she trusts: Silas. Their history crackles under operational shorthand. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Lark
chapters.summary: The assassin Lark receives her contract: three names, including Hale's. We see her methodical, almost tender professionalism. POV: Lark. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy with death.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Silas hides Ada and Hale in a decommissioned motel. Hale reveals DROP's core: a marketplace where governments bid on kill lists, laundered through allied agencies. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the lie he's kept polished begins to rot.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Ferrant pressures Silas to hand over Hale; a British liaison and a foreign attaché make quieter offers. Silas realizes all three governments want the truth buried differently. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: duty revealed as a bidding war.

chapters.title: What Tessa Cost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Silas's failed negotiation, and how DROP used the hostage-taker as a disposable asset. His failure wasn't failure — it was design. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Hale's drive needs a key held in a Geneva vault; meanwhile Lark closes in, having traced Ada's burner. A near-miss firefight forces the group to split. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love rekindling under fire.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Silas does what he does best: negotiates, this time with Ferrant, trading partial access for time. Ferrant hints she may be playing her own game against DROP. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the negotiator becoming the hostage.

chapters.title: Geneva Rain
chapters.summary: Ada retrieves the key in a rain-slicked vault exchange that turns into an ambush; she barely escapes, wounded, with Lark one step behind. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: survival priced in blood.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Lark reports in, and we glimpse DROP's inner auction: bidders from four continents purchasing next quarter's deaths. Hale's name appears on tomorrow's list. POV: Lark. Emotional beat: horror wearing a tailored suit.

chapters.title: Confession at Altitude
chapters.summary: Grounded in a hangar, Silas and Ada finally speak plainly about what they were to each other and what they're willing to lose now. They choose each other, knowing it may be briefly. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love declared against duty.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Priced
chapters.summary: Ferrant sells their location to protect her own family inside DROP's ledger — or so it seems. Lark takes Hale. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath every alliance.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Witness
chapters.summary: Hale, terrified, bargains with his captors using fragments of the drive's contents, buying hours. Silas listens remotely via a bug Ada planted on him weeks ago. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: courage found too late but not wasted.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Silas negotiates Hale's release: himself for the witness. Ada refuses the plan; he goes anyway, walking into Lark's hands with a final gambit hidden in plain speech. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the ultimate negotiation.

chapters.title: Lark's Choice
chapters.summary: Confronted with proof that her own sister was a DROP target sold years ago, Lark hesitates at the trigger. The assassin becomes the wildcard. POV: Lark. Emotional beat: vengeance redirected.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: With Lark turned and Ada running interference, the decrypted DROP archive floods newsrooms and servers worldwide. Three governments scramble; the story can no longer be erased. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: truth escaping its cage.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Ferrant, exposed as a double agent inside DROP, gives Silas the exit she can offer: surrender quietly, testify, disappear. Hale is granted asylum; Lark vanishes into the gray world. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: justice arriving incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: A closed tribunal; Silas tells the whole truth, including Tessa and his own complicity of silence. He accepts prison as the cost of survival with a clean conscience. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Eighteen months later, released early, Silas meets Ada at a small airfield where nothing is classified. A go-bag sits unpacked in his trunk. They board a commercial flight, unremarkable and free. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
